chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār asked Abā Ibrāhīm عليه السلام:
About the sick person who is overcome: should ṭawāf be performed on his behalf around the Kaʿbah? He said: “No; rather, he should be taken around.”

key_terms.الْمَغْلُوبِ: one overcome by weakness or incapacity
key_terms.يُطَافُ بِهِ: he is taken around for tawaf

ai.seo_question: Should tawaf be performed on behalf of a severely ill person, or should he be carried during tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the sick person who is unable to perform tawaf independently. Instead of performing tawaf on his behalf, he is to be physically carried and taken around the Ka'bah himself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2821 - Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Imam Abu Ibrahim (as) about a severely ill person who is unable to perform circumambulation around the Kaaba.
The Imam (as) replied: "No, but he should be carried and circumambulated with."
